<!--
Explain what this step does and why, and copy each command you ran into a
bash chunk. R chunks run from the top of the repository.
-->

Metabolic pathways inferred from the Prokka annotations with MinPath. Commands for this step were run in `minpath/`.

```{bash}
#change directory
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/minpath

#Start by looking at the .tsv file for a single bin
head ../prokka/metabat.5/metabat.5.tsv

#For input to minpath we only want to keep a unique ID for each gene (column 1) and its EC number (column 5). 
head ../prokka/metabat.5/metabat.5.tsv | awk -F '\t' '{print $1,$5}'

# filter the output to only include lines with an EC number
head ../prokka/metabat.5/metabat.5.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{print $1,$5}'

# ensure that the output is tab separated and we also need to remove the header line
head ../prokka/metabat.5/metabat.5.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus'

#This of course only processes the first 10 lines … we need to change head to cat to include all genes
cat ../prokka/metabat.5/metabat.5.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus'

# Finally we send the output to a file so that it can be used as input to minpath
cat ../prokka/metabat.5/metabat.5.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus' > metabat.5.ec

# run minpath on this file as follows;
minpath -ec metabat.5.ec -report metabat.5.ec.report -details metabat.5.ec.details

# look at the top few lines of output
head metabat.5.ec.report 

#EXAMPLE
  ##  path PWY-7321 any n/a  naive 1  minpath 1  fam0  4  fam-found  2  name  ecdysteroid metabolism (arthropods)
  ## PWY-7321 which is a pathway identifier in the metacyc database. You can use this to lookup the full pathway. Eg PWY-7321
  ## naive 1 tells us that at least one gene from this pathway was found. Simply calling a pathway present whenever one of its genes is found is the “naive” approach
  ## minpath 1 tells us that minpath kept this pathway in its minimal set of pathways. If this says minpath 0 then minpath decided that the genes found are better explained by other pathways, so the evidence for this one is weak
  ## fam0 4 tells us that four gene families are involved in this pathway
  ## fam-found 2 tells us that we found 2 gene families from the pathway in this genome
  ## name ecdysteroid metabolism (arthropods) is a name for the pathway
```

```{bash}
#look for job
tail ../prokka/slurm-486.out

#run the following code to prepare minpath inputs for all bins.
while read bin;do 
  cat ../prokka/$bin/${bin}.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{printf("%s\t%s\n", $1,$5)}' | grep -v '^locus' > ${bin}.ec 
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

#Now run minpath on every bin. 
while read bin;do 
  minpath -ec ${bin}.ec -report ${bin}.ec.report -details ${bin}.ec.details
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

# The first pathway is named photosynthesis light reactions and has the metacyc code PWY-101. This pathway includes the essential components of photosynthesis that occur in light, Photosystem I and Photosystem II.
# Use the following command to search for this pathway across all the bins
grep 'PWY-101' *.ec.report
```

Question 4.1
How many bins contain at least one gene from this pathway?
  5 bins:
    - contig_118
    - metabat.38
    - metabat.4
    - metabat.51
    - metabat.64

Which bin has all of the genes (ie a complete pathway)?
  metabat.64  ->  fam-found  4

For which bins does minpath keep the pathway (minpath 1)?
  3 bins:
    - metabat.38
    - metabat.51
    - metabat.64

```{bash}
#Cross reference your results with the output from gtdbtk to see the taxonomy of bins containing this pathway.
grep 'metabat.26' ../gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv

grep 'PWY-5360' *.ec.report
```

Question 4.2
How many bins contain the pathway PWY-5360?
  1 bin:
    - metabat.3

What order (in a taxonomic sense) do these bins belong to? Are they in the same family?
  metabat.3 is classified as:
    - Order: Campylobacterales
    - Family: Arcobacteraceae
    - Genus: Halarcobacter
  
How strong is the evidence that these bins really have this pathway? Look at the fam-found and minpath columns.
  The evidence is weak:
    - fam0 3 – The pathway is expected to contain 3 gene families.
    - fam-found 1 – Only 1 of the 3 gene families was detected.
    - minpath 0 – MinPath does not retain this pathway.
